title: Rank a list without sorting it

screens.prompt: Put Ada's place in the team into C2, fastest first, without sorting the sheet.

hints.syntax: RANK takes the value, then the whole column: =RANK(B2,B2:B6).
hints.func-rank: Counting how many times are faster is a formula of its own — RANK does exactly that.
hints.require-ref: The second argument should be the range B2:B6, not a hand-typed list.
hints.value: Only Ben's 61 is faster than 58, so Ada is second.
hints.error: Dividing by zero anywhere in the formula leaves #DIV/0!.

reject.why: right arithmetic, wrong tool — the sheet should say rank, not count-if-plus-one
the third argument reverses the order, so Ada is ranked fourth-slowest instead
Ben's place, 1, sitting in Ada's row
the range excludes B2, so the fast times are outside the ranking
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
the missing comma means the arguments never separate

screens.prompt: The slowest swimmer gets the place number 1, so put Ada's place on that scale into C2.

hints.syntax: The third argument is the order, and any nonzero value means ascending: =RANK(B2,B2:B6,1).
hints.func-rank: This is the same ranking read from the other end, and RANK takes an order argument.
hints.require-ref: Rank against the whole column B2:B6, so every swimmer is in the comparison.
hints.value: Ascending, the places run 50, 55, 57, 58, 61 — Ada's 58 is fourth from the bottom, so place 4.
hints.error: Dividing by zero leaves #DIV/0! instead of a place.

reject.why: the descending place, 2, not the ascending one
Ben's ascending place, 5, in Ada's row
the range leaves out B2, so two swimmers are missing from the comparison
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
the missing commas jam three arguments into one
the second smallest time, 55, which is a value rather than a place
twice the ascending place, 8, which is not a place at all

docs.explain: RANK answers a question sorting cannot: as you read each row, where does this one sit among all of them. Sorting the sheet answers it once and then loses the original order, and a saved sort is a change to the data rather than a calculation about it. RANK compares the value against a fixed range and counts how many are greater. The range must be anchored — `$B$2:$B$6` or at least the column locked — because the moment the formula is filled down, an unanchored reference slides with it and every row ends up ranking against a different slice. The optional third argument flips the direction: 0 or omitted ranks largest-first, any nonzero value ranks smallest-first. Equal values share a rank and then the next rank is skipped, so two swimmers tied at the top are both 1 and nobody is 2 — positions and ranks are not the same thing, and a report that pretends otherwise will not add up. RANK.EQ behaves the same way; RANK.AVG is the variant that shares the average of the tied places.

errors.text: The value being ranked does not appear in the range it is being ranked against.
The number argument was text that cannot be read as a number, so no comparison was possible.
The rank was divided by zero downstream, so the cell shows that error instead.

docs.atWork: A league table that shows each swimmer's place on the row they already occupy, and the same sheet ranked slowest-first for handicap purposes.
docs.outcome: Put a place number on every row of an unsorted list, in either direction.
docs.teaches: RANK, and anchoring the range it compares against
docs.dataset: A team of swim times ranked both ways
